sections.name: Red Bulborb
sections.card:
Summary: The best-known enemy in the series, a big grub-dog with a red back and white spots, called the Spotty Bulborb in the first game and the Red Bulborb in Pikmin 2. It sleeps in the open by day, wakes when it is attacked or when something is carried right next to it, and then lunges at Pikmin and leaders to eat them.
Weak points: Purple Pikmin do serious damage, especially when their landing stuns it. A big crowd hitting it at the same moment gets thrown off, and it goes back to trying to eat.
Tips: With 30 or more Pikmin, keep throwing them onto its back one after another and accept that some get shaken off; that beats swarming it. With a very small army, wake it and run it far from where it sleeps. It turns and heads home, and the moment it lies down again you get a few seconds in which it can neither move nor harm you. A Bulborb woken by mistake before your Pikmin have attacked: retreat until it turns around, then start a fresh attack run. Some caves themed on metal let you get rid of it for good: wake it, then quickly circle the hole in the sublevel, and it falls off the stage.

sections.name: Dwarf Red Bulborb
sections.card:
Summary: A small, common enemy called the Dwarf Red Bulborb in Pikmin 2. It looks like a young bulborb but is really a breadbug copying a bulborb's look. It barks and chases when it spots a leader or Pikmin, bites one Pikmin at a time and chews it slowly, and never strays far from its territory.
Weak points: A single Pikmin thrown onto its back kills it, and its low health means swarming works too. Killing it while it chews frees the Pikmin it caught. Purple Pikmin are exceptionally effective: they steer onto a nearby enemy when thrown, and quick throws at a group stun the whole group and likely kill most of it.
Tips: It is no threat alone; the danger is numbers, or a dwarf standing next to other enemies, so deal with the dwarfs first in a mixed fight. Purples work well on a crowd, as on the eighth sublevel of the Cavern of Chaos. In Pikmin 2 it does not call for help: the scream that wakes a nearby bulborb happens only in the first game. If you lead it past its range it gives up and walks home.

sections.name: Fiery Blowhog
sections.card:
Summary: A pig with a red snout that breathes fire, and one of the common enemies in Pikmin 2. It potters about in a tiny area. When it sees a leader or Pikmin it swings round and sends out a jet of flame, and if Pikmin cling to it, it throws them off to the front of it and flames that spot.
Weak points: Throw Purple Pikmin at it: they hurt it badly and stop it throwing Pikmin off or breathing fire. In Pikmin 2 it is also weak enough that a large group can simply rush it. To dodge the flame, run as soon as you see it start to breathe in; there is a short delay before it fires, and from the start of that breath until the fire ends it is rooted and aimed, so anyone who has moved away is not followed.
Tips: Any Pikmin type can beat it. Pikmin clinging to it cannot be set alight and Red Pikmin ignore fire; the page warns that being bucked into water is what can kill them, so turn it away from water first. In Pikmin 2 a Blowhog may not fire when only a leader is close to it.

sections.name: Wollywog (white)
sections.card:
Summary: A large, flatter-bodied white frog found underground, called the Wollyhop on the wiki and the Wollywog in some games and regions. It is passive until a leader or Pikmin comes close, then leaps and lands on them, and the landing kills every Pikmin within a wide radius.
Weak points: Purple Pikmin slams do large damage and may briefly stun it. Swarming works less well in Pikmin 2 than in the first game, so throw Pikmin onto it instead of sending them all in.
Tips: While it is airborne, whistle your Pikmin away before it comes down; otherwise they get thrown off and may lose their growth stage. Killing it just as it is about to drop does not help the Pikmin underneath, who are still crushed.

sections.name: Ultra-spicy spray
sections.card:
Summary: The red spray, made by gathering ten ultra-spicy berries from Burgeoning Spiderworts or from a concentrated dose of spray nectar. In Pikmin 2 it makes every Pikmin in the current leader's squad faster and quicker at its jobs for 40 seconds, however far away they are.
Uses: Sprayed Pikmin move almost as quickly as flowered White Pikmin, and all their work speeds up: hitting, breaking gates, building bridges and recovering from a knockdown. In Pikmin 2 a flashing pink light takes the place of the leaf, bud or flower, and all the spray really does is make them act like flower Pikmin, so using it on a squad that is already all flowers gets you nothing. Their attack power becomes the same for every colour, so Purple Pikmin hit weaker while sprayed. A Pikmin that jumps at its target before hitting, instead of latching on, is not sped up.
Tips: Spraying already-spicy Pikmin restarts the 40 seconds, and so does an ultra-bitter spray. Pikmin that go into an Onion or the ship lose the effect, and Pikmin that are drowning die faster. If the effect runs out while Pikmin are hauling something, they keep the boosted carrying speed until the object is delivered or dropped, which helps with the Doomsday Apparatus. The Awakening Wood is the place to gather lots of berries.

sections.name: Ultra-bitter spray
sections.card:
Summary: The purple spray: collect ten berries from the purple Burgeoning Spiderworts, or find it as a concentrated dose. Point the cursor at an enemy or a bomb rock and it stops moving and gradually turns to stone. In all this lasts nine seconds: one for the stone to form, then eight fully encased.
Uses: Petrifying an enemy that is eating Pikmin saves them, and a bomb rock in mid-countdown freezes, giving you time to run. The enemy shakes just before it breaks free. While it is stone, ordinary Pikmin attacks and leader punches do 1.5 times damage to most enemies, but only a quarter to bosses such as the Empress Bulblax, Man-at-Legs and Beady Long Legs, almost nothing to the Bloysters (0.03 times), and half to the Titan Dweevil, which can only be hurt when unarmed. A Purple Pikmin's stomp and a bomb rock's damage stay the same either way.
Tips: Aim before you press: with no enemy near, the dose is wasted. It is rarer than the spicy spray: fewer berry plants carry it, and you find it only after getting White Pikmin, near the Bulblax Kingdom. A petrified Bumbling Snitchbug drops the leader it was holding. An enemy killed while it is stone crumbles and leaves drops of nectar or spray, and a Titan Dweevil killed that way drops 10 random sprays.

sections.name: Nectar
sections.card:
Summary: A large drop of liquid that turns leaf and bud Pikmin into flowers. A leaf or bud Pikmin that comes across a drop on the ground kneels and drinks for about two seconds, whether it was idle or sent over, then springs up with a flower on its head.
Uses: In Pikmin 2 any number of Pikmin can share a single drop, but it starts to shrink as soon as the first one begins drinking and has vanished by the time that one is done, so only Pikmin that start drinking during that window become flowers. The window is longer in Pikmin 2 than in the first game. The best way to flower many at once is to get them to swarm in a tight group.
Tips: The wiki lists nectar weed patches, piles of rubble, eggs, Honeywisps, Mitites, Bulborb Larvae and petrified enemies among the sources; most give a single drop and sometimes more.

sections.name: Eggs (nectar eggs)
sections.card:
Summary: A white, roundish object sitting in cave alcoves and at a few places on the surface. Attack it and it breaks open and releases nectar, or sometimes other things, including living creatures. In Pikmin 2 the eggs that Honeywisps hold work the same as eggs on the ground.
Uses: Break one and you get, by chance: a single drop of nectar (50 percent), two drops (35 percent), a drop of ultra-bitter spray (5 percent), a drop of ultra-spicy spray (5 percent) or a group of ten Mitites (5 percent). The roll happens at the instant it breaks, not when it appears, and in story mode a spray you have not unlocked yet comes out as a single drop of nectar.
Tips: You can break one with Pikmin, with leader punches, or with an enemy projectile such as a Gatling Groink's mortars. A Purple Pikmin thrown at it breaks it at once and defeats any Mitites inside straight away. Using a leader is also recommended, because a thrown Pikmin that is called back may drink the nectar and waste it.

sections.name: Blue Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The only permanent Pikmin type that can safely go into water; the other types flail in panic and drown. In Pikmin 2 five are found in the Awakening Wood, chasing Wolpoles beyond an electric gate that you break down with Yellow Pikmin.
Uses: Blues are required for the Shower Room, whose entrance is clogged underwater; for the Submerged Castle, whose entrance is under the surface and which no other type can enter, exploits included; and for the second half of the Valley of Repose, where they have to break a white bramble gate and a clog a little way past the Emergence Cave, which opens the Subterranean Complex and the Frontier Cavern. Seesaw blocks under water work only for Blue Pikmin.
Tips: In Pikmin 2 an idle Blue Pikmin that sees a Pikmin drowning nearby runs in, picks it up and throws it to shore, unless the drowning one is too far away. They can also lift a Purple Pikmin out of water. Otherwise their attack, toughness and speed are about average, though in Pikmin 2 they die more often than any other type.

sections.name: Yellow Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The Pikmin with big ears, which get thrown higher than any other type, so they reach high ledges and can cling to the Beady Long Legs. In Pikmin 2 electricity cannot hurt them. Five wait in the Perplexing Pool near the middle of the map; getting to them takes White Pikmin, and a Fiery Bulblax stands at the entrance of their Onion.
Uses: Only Yellow Pikmin can destroy the electric gate in front of the Blue Onion, and they handle electric enemies and hazards that kill other types on contact. None of it is strictly required: no task in Pikmin 2 needs them exclusively. Their old bomb-rock carrying does not work in Pikmin 2, where bomb rocks are only a hazard.
Tips: They are recommended against a pair of Anode Beetles, which make a line of electricity that fatally shocks any non-Yellow Pikmin touching it; against Anode Dweevils, which shock every non-Yellow Pikmin under them after being attacked; and against the Titan Dweevil's electric weapon.

sections.name: Purple Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: Purple Pikmin have the strength of ten Pikmin. They are first found at a pair of Violet Candypop Buds in the Emergence Cave, where a treasure that needs 101 Pikmin to lift is waiting.
Uses: Purple Pikmin are what you need for the heavy treasures. The Spherical Atlas, the first treasure that opens a new area, takes 101 Pikmin to carry, so some Purples must help; the Geographic Projection is the same; the Doomsday Apparatus takes 1000 Pikmin or only 100 Purples. The Professional Noisemaker sits inside the Waterwraith, which is invulnerable until Purple Pikmin stomp on it. To build a big Purple crowd, go to sublevel 8 of the Subterranean Complex, which has an exit geyser, Candypop Buds and some eggs: there, spend the Queen Candypop Buds before the Violet ones and you end up with 15 Purples and 2 Pikmin of another type.
Tips: On most enemies a landing Purple stuns about one time in three, and the stun lasts a full five seconds. A small homing effect bends its fall onto a nearby enemy, so the aim need not be exact. The landing also kills small, fragile enemies such as Shearwigs and Dwarf Bulborbs, breaks nectar eggs at once, defeats Mitites in a wide radius, switches off fire geysers and electric wires, and counts as an attack, so it damages poison emitters and Fiery Bulblaxes. They do not panic at Mitites or at an Emperor Bulblax's roar. The cost: they are slow, slower still when carrying, and a few bosses resist stunning or cannot be stunned.

sections.name: White Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The smallest and fastest Pikmin, whose flowered form keeps up with a leader wearing Rush Boots, or beats one. Their red eyes let them find treasure that is completely buried underground. In Pikmin 2 you make them by throwing Pikmin into the Ivory Candypop Buds on the third sublevel of the White Flower Garden.
Uses: Needed for every fully buried treasure: no other type can do it, exploits included. They also stand through poison gas without choking, so they matter when destroying poison emitters, though other types can do it with difficulty. The page recommends them, though they are not strictly needed, against the Doodlebug, the Munge Dweevil and the Titan Dweevil's poison weapon, and for treasures behind poison-emitter gates such as the Seed of Greed, the Anti-hiccup Fungus and the Geographic Projection.
Tips: Being eaten does not save a White Pikmin, but it does hurt the eater, which is poisoned and takes damage at once, often enough to kill a small enemy such as a Dwarf Orange Bulborb. Treat that as a last resort. In Pikmin 2 a White Pikmin hits as hard as the ordinary colours.

sections.name: Red Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The Pikmin you meet first in every game. Pointy noses give them 1.5 times the attack power of most types, and they ignore fire. In Pikmin 2 the first five are in the Valley of Repose, in the middle of a fight with a Dwarf Red Bulborb, and Olimar lands beside them.
Uses: Nothing in Pikmin 2 strictly needs Red Pikmin, but as the first type you find they are the ones you must use until another type turns up. The Fiery Bulblax is their main job, because only Reds can stand its flames. The other ways in are to find it submerged, which puts its fire out, to land Purple Pikmin on it, to let it eat White Pikmin so they poison it, or, in certain caves, to lure it into the abyss. Where no water is around to beat a Fiery Bulblax another way, Reds are the intended answer, as for the Essence of Despair, the Frosty Bauble, the Gemstar Wife and the Insect Condo. They are also intended for the Gyroid Bust, to carry it through fire geysers unless the geysers are destroyed.
Tips: Their fire immunity matters less in Pikmin 2 than in other games: any Pikmin can destroy fire geysers, Fiery Blowhogs fall easily to Purple Pikmin, and Fiery Dweevils and the Titan Dweevil's flame weapon can be beaten with any type. In 2-Player Battle, player 1 gets Red Pikmin and player 2 gets Blue Pikmin with the same 1.5 times attack power.
